questions.stem: The pH of pure water at 25 °C is exactly:
questions.explanation: Pure water at 25 °C is neutral: [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ mol/L, so pH = 7. Acidic solutions have pH < 7 (higher H⁺), basic solutions pH > 7. The scale runs 0-14. A change of one pH unit means a ten-fold change in H⁺ concentration.

questions.stem: Litmus paper turns red in the presence of:
questions.explanation: Blue litmus turns red in acids; red litmus turns blue in bases. Litmus is a mixture of dyes from lichens. Other indicators: phenolphthalein — colourless in acid, pink in base; methyl orange — red in acid, yellow in base; turmeric — yellow in acid/neutral, red in base.

questions.stem: Common salt used in cooking has the chemical formula:
questions.explanation: Common (table) salt is sodium chloride, NaCl. The other options are: NaHCO₃ — baking soda; Na₂CO₃ — washing soda; NaOH — caustic soda (a strong base). Most table salt in India is fortified with potassium iodate to prevent iodine-deficiency goitre.

questions.stem: A neutralisation reaction between an acid and a base produces:
questions.explanation: Acid + Base → Salt + Water. Example: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Acid + active metal gives salt + H₂; metal oxide (basic) + acid also gives salt + water. Neutralisation is exothermic — the mixture warms up slightly.

questions.stem: The acid secreted by the stomach during digestion is:
questions.explanation: Parietal cells of the stomach lining secrete hydrochloric acid, giving gastric juice a pH of around 1.5-3.5. It kills microbes and activates pepsin from pepsinogen. Antacids (milk of magnesia = Mg(OH)₂, or baking soda) neutralise excess HCl. Citric acid is found in citrus fruits; acetic acid in vinegar; sulphuric acid in lead-acid car batteries.

questions.stem: Match the common name with the chemical formula. A. Baking soda. B. Washing soda. C. Caustic soda. D. Plaster of Paris. List-II: 1. NaOH, 2. Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, 3. NaHCO₃, 4. CaSO₄·½H₂O.
questions.explanation: Baking soda — sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃). Washing soda — hydrated sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O). Caustic soda — sodium hydroxide (NaOH), a strong base used in soap-making. Plaster of Paris — calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO₄·½H₂O); made by heating gypsum to ~120 °C.

questions.stem: Which acid is naturally present in sour milk and curd?
questions.explanation: Lactic acid is produced when Lactobacillus bacteria ferment lactose in milk; it curdles the milk and gives curd its sour taste. Citric acid is in lemons and oranges; formic acid in ant stings and nettles; tartaric acid in grapes and tamarind; acetic acid in vinegar; oxalic acid in spinach.
